topic: US sanctions context and post-Maduro shift bearing on Venezuelan LNG export prospects (2024-2026)
wiki_text: Venezuela holds large gas reserves but has never built an LNG export facility; successive proposals (Cristobal Colon/Project Venezuela LNG, Delta Caribe Oriental/CIGMA, the PDVSA-Rosneft offshore project, and Sycar's FLNG) have all stalled. US sanctions are the dominant constraint: after a brief 2023 easing, the US reinstated broad sanctions on Venezuela's oil and gas sector in April 2024, which contemporaries judged to have effectively killed the Sycar FLNG plan, and any export development would require an OFAC license. The political landscape shifted sharply in early 2026: President Nicolas Maduro was captured/arrested on 3 January 2026 and an interim government formed; US Energy Secretary Chris Wright visited on 11 February 2026 to survey oil and gas infrastructure, and on 29 January 2026 Venezuela enacted an amended Organic Hydrocarbons Law. As of this sweep, however, the near-term gas focus is the Trinidad-piped Dragon field (where Shell received conditional OFAC approval to resume planning before Venezuela suspended energy agreements with Trinidad) rather than any domestic LNG liquefaction terminal. None of GEM's four Venezuelan LNG export terminals showed signs of revival, so their cancelled/shelved statuses are retained.
